column1: # The level 0 swipe corpus (beads tla-7xql.2, tla-7xql.7 and tla-7xql.8,
# 240 items over the five templates in swipe/level0/TEMPLATES.tsv, 48 per
# template. Every claim is a CONSTANT-level TLA+ expression: no variable, no
# prime, no temporal operator. That is what lets this rung run with no model
# screen at all, which is the whole reason the epic picks level 0 first.
# Rows are tab-delimited and carry the literal marker ITEM in field 1, so prose
# in this file can never be read as data. Read rows with awk -F'\t' or cut,
# never with IFS=$'\t' read: tab is IFS whitespace, so a run of tabs collapses
# AN ITEM ROW. Eleven fields, in order:
#    3  template   T1-T5, resolving to a TEMPLATES.tsv row
#    4  ask        the tag shown WITH the question: holds or implies
#    5  kind       the item's own kind: true, false, vacuous, illformed
#                  or unparsed. unparsed is a SANY parse failure and landed
#    6  swipe      right, left or down. Derived from field 5 by the bake
#    7  rc_claim   the exit code of ASSUME (claim). Written by the bake
#    8  rc_wf      the exit code of ASSUME ((claim) \/ ~(claim)). Same
#    9  claim      the single line the reader sees
#   10  vacuity    a level 0 witness that the claim is vacuous, or -
#   11  flash      the one line shown after the swipe, always present. On a
#                  false, vacuous or illformed item it is the correction. On a
#                  true item it is the reason the claim holds, because there is
#                  nothing to correct about a true statement. Frank ruled on
# FIELDS 6, 7 AND 8 ARE OWNED BY swipe/level0/bake.sh. Do not hand-edit them.
# `bake.sh --write` measures them with TLC and writes them back, `bake.sh
# --check` confirms them, and harness/test-swipe-level0.sh gates the result.
# Fields 4, 5, 9, 10 and 11 are authored, and field 5 is the author's
# PREDICTION, which the bake is there to contradict. It contradicted three of
# the first eighty items and nine of the next hundred and sixty.
# WHY FIELD 4 AND FIELD 5 ARE SEPARATE, which is a finding rather than a
# preference. Decision D5 on the epic says the item's kind is tagged in the
# question, and decision D3 says the kind is kept in the data so accuracy can
# be split by it. Those cannot be the same column: D3's kind IS the answer, so
# showing it with the question gives the item away. So field 4 is the tag the
# reader sees, naming which of the epic's question kinds this line is, and
# field 5 is the kind the data keeps. See swipe/README.md.
# Frank ruled on 2026-10-18 that the split stands and D5 wants rewording rather
# than reversing. The corpus was already built this way, so the ruling changes
# the contract's wording and no row.
# FIELD 10 MAKES VACUITY A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A CLAIM. A vacuous item and
# a plainly true one both exit 0, so TLC alone cannot tell them apart. The
# witness is a second level 0 expression that holds exactly when the item is
# vacuous, and the bake runs it in the same batch, so the vacuous label has a
# ITEMS ARE AUTHORED IN MATCHED GROUPS, AND THAT IS WHAT KEEPS THE STEM-BLIND
# GATE GREEN. The unit is either a four, one item of each kind built from one
# idea, or a pair, a true and a false item built from one idea. Six fours and
# twelve pairs is 48, and it landed the mix at 18 true, 18 false, 6 vacuous and
# 6 illformed without anybody counting. A few groups came apart when the bake
# contradicted a label or the probe named a token, so the file is not six
# clean fours and twelve clean pairs today.
# THE MIX IS 18 TRUE, 18 FALSE, 6 VACUOUS, 5 ILLFORMED AND 1 UNPARSED NOW, per
# template, and the arithmetic that matters did not move. illformed and
# unparsed both bake to down, so the swipe mix is still 18 right, 18 left and
# 12 down, and the base rate is still 18 of 48, which is 0.3750. That is why
# bead tla-7xql.11 CONVERTED five illformed rows rather than adding five rows:
# adding would have moved n, the base rate and the whole power table in
# swipe/README.md together. swipe/README.md names the five rows and says what
# each conversion cost the group it came out of.
# A token that enters inside a matched group carries that group's label
# distribution, so a decision stump over the claim surface learns nothing from
# it. A token unique to one member sits on one item, and the probe's
# leave-one-out scoring already makes a one-item rule worthless. The ids no
# longer run in kind order because of this: ids are never renumbered, so the
# items added in tla-7xql.7 took 17 to 48, and rows sit in their authoring
# groups so a reviewer sees a matched pair side by side.
# THERE IS NO VACUITY SENTINEL AND THERE MUST NOT BE ONE. The first eighty
# items marked a vacuous body with 99, on five items, every one of them
# vacuous, and two of those sat in T1. A reader who learns that a 99 means
# swipe down never evaluates another vacuous item. The bodies are ordinary
# claims now, and the lesson of a vacuous universal is the empty range rather
# than anything in the body. Varying the sentinel per template would be five
# rules in place of one, not a fix.
# PARENTHESIZE EVERY NEGATIVE LITERAL, and that is a finding rather than a
# taste. The jar's own Naturals.tla states the contract:
#   a % b  and  a \div b  are defined so that for any integers  a  and  b
#   with  b > 0 , the following formula is true:
# TLC 2026.07.31.184830 holds to it. Measured through tlc2.REPL on 2026-10-20:
# The quotient rounds down, which is what the contract asks for.
# WHAT BITES IS PRECEDENCE. Prefix minus sits at 12-12, \div at 13-13 and % at
# 10-11, so \div binds tighter than the minus sign and % binds looser. Drop the
# parentheses and the two halves of one identity group different ways:
# -17 \div 5 parses as -(17 \div 5) and reads -3, while -17 % 5 parses as
# (-17) % 5 and reads 3. Then 5 * -3 + 3 is -12 and the contract looks broken.
# -9 \div 4 = -2 against (-9) \div 4 = -3 goes the same way, as does
# -7 \div 3 = -2 against (-7) \div 3 = -3. Exponent carries it too: -2 ^ 2 is
# -4 and (-2) ^ 2 is 4. So the rule covers ^ as well as \div, and an item
# written without the parentheses teaches a precedence trap while claiming to
# THIS HEADER USED TO READ "NO ITEM MAY DEPEND ON \div WITH A NEGATIVE
# DIVIDEND", on the reading that TLC broke the identity and an item over
# -17 \div 5 would ship a falsehood. The conclusion was right and the premise
# was not. Three authored items were replaced rather than re-labeled on that
# premise, which nobody needs to undo, and the constraint relaxes to the
# parenthesizing rule above. Whoever reads the old reading somewhere else
# should not take it for a live measurement. Bead tla-mv4b settled it and
# THE REAL DIVERGENCE IS A NEGATIVE DIVISOR, and no item goes near it.
# Naturals.tla defines the pair through a witness in 0..(b-1), and that
# interval is empty once b goes negative, so the module says nothing and TLC
# answers anyway: 5 \div (-2) is -3, and 5 % (-2) raises. Upstream tlaplus#721,
# open since 2022. harness/test-swipe-level0.sh pins both halves, so the day
# upstream closes it that suite goes red and this note can go.
# T5's declared trap IS a negative operand, so growing it runs at this. Every
# dividend here is non-negative and every divisor is positive. The negative
# operands sit on %, on + and -, on intervals like -3..3, on \in Int, and on
# A CLAIM SANY REFUSES COMES BACK (150, 150), AND IT IS THE FOURTH ROW IN THE
# CHANNEL. Six of the items authored for tla-7xql.7 landed there, and the
# cause was the same every time: two operators from one precedence band that
# do not associate with each other, as in 12 \div 2 * 3, TRUE \/ FALSE /\
# FALSE, and 12 % 5 + 12 \div 5. Parentheses fix all three. Those six were
# replaced with claims that parse, because at the time the row was not
# IT IS SETTLED NOW. Frank ruled on 2026-10-18, bead tla-7xql.10, that a parse
# failure is a down-swipe item under its own kind, unparsed, and on bead
# tla-7xql.11 that the corpus gains those items by CONVERSION rather than by
# addition. Five rows carry the kind today, one per template, and each is a
# trap in its own template's subject matter rather than a precedence item
# wearing another label. The lesson the row teaches is that TLC never ran: SANY
# refuses the module, so the pair is one fact reported twice rather than two
# readings that agree. Section 11 of harness/test-swipe-level0.sh is what keeps
# a channel row from shipping with no item behind it again.
# FIELD 11 IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IT IS NOT DECORATION. Measured on this task
# shape and recorded as L2 on the epic: a falsehood is reproduced later at .19
# with no feedback, .15 with a bare verdict, and .04 with the verdict plus the
# corrected claim. A bare verdict sits on the measured floor, so every row
# AND THE .04 COVERS 150 OF THE 240 ROWS, NOT ALL OF THEM. L2 measured whether
# a FALSEHOOD comes back, so it speaks to the 90 false, 30 vacuous, 25
# illformed and 5 unparsed items, which have something to correct. An unparsed
# item is corrected by a pair of parentheses rather than by a new value, and
# that is still a correction. The 90 true items have no
# corrected claim, only a reason they hold, and nothing measured says .04
# carries to them. So field 11 stays required on every row and the number
# attached to it does not. Frank ruled on 2026-10-18.
